question: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg increases diuresis because:

options.opb: Decreases the peritubular reabsorption of water.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg -> increases hydrostatic pressure in the glomerulus -> enhances glomerular filtration rate -> increases urine production -> increases diuresis -> 80%
CHAIN: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg -> leads to constriction of the efferent arteriole -> increases glomerular filtration rate -> promotes diuresis -> 75%

CHAIN: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg -> causes dilation of the afferent arteriole -> increases glomerular perfusion pressure -> enhances glomerular filtration rate -> promotes diuresis -> 70%
enhanced_information: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg leads to enhanced glomerular filtration rate, promoting diuresis. The efferent arteriole constriction and afferent arteriole dilation contribute to this effect by increasing glomerular perfusion pressure. The evidence paths confirm the relationship between the kidney glomerulus and glomerular filtration rate, supporting the consensus-aligned reasoning.
analysis: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg can lead to enhanced glomerular filtration rate, promoting diuresis. The efferent arteriole constriction and afferent arteriole dilation contribute to this effect by increasing glomerular perfusion pressure. This aligns with the known physiological response of the kidneys to changes in blood pressure. The enhanced information provided further supports the consensus-aligned reasoning.
